rationale: A wins because it knows when to stop. It gives three usable lanes and correctly pushes “A profitable public company takes on Tesla's cash-hungry energy business” into refused angles; B promotes the same thin material as “A profitable charger maker bets on a capital-heavy market,” then admits “Right now the facts support only ‘large, profitable, publicly traded,’ which is a description, not a story.” That is the sort of extra angle founders mistake for permission to pitch.
gaps_in_A: “Story type: category-creation” is the wrong label. Anker is not creating a category; this is a brand-extension or company-strategy angle.
“purchase measured in thousands of dollars and decades on the wall” imports price scale and product lifetime that were not in the supplied update. Plausible is not the same as sourced.
“cash-hungry energy business” appears only in a refused angle, but it is still an invented editorial jab. Reject it for grounding, not just duplication.
gaps_in_B: “A profitable charger maker bets on a capital-heavy market” should be conditional or refused, not promoted as a main angle. The set itself says the current facts are “a description, not a story.”
“Story type: trend” contradicts its own caution. One Anker launch is not a trend unless the user supplies evidence of comparable consumer-electronics moves.

“demands installer networks, long warranties, and service obligations it has never carried at this scale” overreaches beyond the update. The missing warranty and installer details are proof gaps, not established burdens.
“The prevailing belief is that whole-home batteries mean panel work, transfer switches, and an electrician's week” is useful reporting context, but stated too confidently from facts not supplied.
